claim: SOX4 is the 17th highest expressed transcription factor in human endometrial stromal cells.
source: We noted that among the transcription factors expressed in endometrium stromal cells, SOX4 was the 17th highest expressed (Figure 1A)
evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data showing expression levels of transcription factors in HESCs, visualized in Figure 1A

claim: SOX4 is the most abundant member of the SOX family in human endometrial stromal cells.
source: We noted that among the transcription factors expressed in endometrium stromal cells, SOX4 was the 17th highest expressed (Figure 1A), and as the most abundant member in SOX family (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data showing expression of SOX family genes in HESCs, visualized in Figure 1B

claim: SOX4 expression is the most abundant SOX family member in mouse stromal cells.
source: Meanwhile, previous RNA-Seq data in isolated mouse stromal and epithelial cells revealed that SOX4 expression was the most abundant SOX family in stromal cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Supported by previous RNA-Seq data from isolated mouse cells, referenced in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: SOX17 expression is restricted to the epithelium in mouse uterus.
source: while the expression of SOX17 was restricted to the epithelium (Deng et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Deng et al., 2019

claim: SOX4 is detected at low levels in the E2-dominant proliferative phase of the menstrual cycle.
source: Albeit SOX4 was detected at a low level in the E2-dominant proliferative phase, its expression was progressively increased in the nucleus of stromal cellsin P4-dominant early, middle, late secretory phases and this high expression in stroma cell sustained in the decidual cells in early pregnancy (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: SOX4 expression progressively increases in the nucleus of stromal cells during P4-dominant early, middle, and late secretory phases.
source: Albeit SOX4 was detected at a low level in the E2-dominant proliferative phase, its expression was progressively increased in the nucleus of stromal cellsin P4-dominant early, middle, late secretory phases and this high expression in stroma cell sustained in the decidual cells in early pregnancy (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: High SOX4 expression in stromal cells is sustained in decidual cells in early pregnancy.
source: Albeit SOX4 was detected at a low level in the E2-dominant proliferative phase, its expression was progressively increased in the nucleus of stromal cellsin P4-dominant early, middle, late secretory phases and this high expression in stroma cell sustained in the decidual cells in early pregnancy (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: SOX4 mRNA levels are gradually increased in immortalized HESCs after EPC treatment.
source: This upregulation of SOX4 in differentiated stromal cell in secretory phase was also substantiated in in vitro decidualized stromal cells induced by E2, MPA, and cAMP (EPC) cocktail, displaying gradually cumulated mRNA and protein levels in immortalized HESCs (Figure 1D, E)
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D

claim: SOX4 protein levels are gradually increased in immortalized HESCs after EPC treatment.
source: This upregulation of SOX4 in differentiated stromal cell in secretory phase was also substantiated in in vitro decidualized stromal cells induced by E2, MPA, and cAMP (EPC) cocktail, displaying gradually cumulated mRNA and protein levels in immortalized HESCs (Figure 1D, E)
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1E

claim: SOX4 mRNA and protein levels are increased in primary stromal cells after EPC treatment.
source: This upregulation of SOX4 in differentiated stromal cell in secretory phase was also substantiated in in vitro decidualized stromal cells induced by E2, MPA, and cAMP (EPC) cocktail, displaying gradually cumulated mRNA and protein levels in immortalized HESCs (Figure 1D, E) as well as in primary stromal cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B

claim: SOX4 is mainly localized in the nucleus of HESCs after EPC treatment.
source: Immunofluorescence also manifested that SOX4 was mainly localized in the nucleus of HESCs after EPC treatment (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F

claim: SOX4 expression is induced by 2 days treatment of MPA.
source: This assumption was supported by the observation that SOX4 expression was induced by 2 days treatment of MPA, a progesterone analog commonly used in decidualization induction, and abrogated in the presence of PGR antagonist RU486 (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A

claim: SOX4 expression induced by MPA is abrogated in the presence of PGR antagonist RU486.
source: This assumption was supported by the observation that SOX4 expression was induced by 2 days treatment of MPA, a progesterone analog commonly used in decidualization induction, and abrogated in the presence of PGR antagonist RU486 (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Progesterone-induced SOX4 mRNA levels are significantly attenuated with PGR knockdown in immortalized HESCs.
source: Progesterone-induced SOX4 mRNA and protein levels were significantly attenuated with PGR knockdown in immortalized HESCs (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C

claim: Progesterone-induced SOX4 protein levels are significantly attenuated with PGR knockdown in immortalized HESCs.
source: Progesterone-induced SOX4 mRNA and protein levels were significantly attenuated with PGR knockdown in immortalized HESCs (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2D

claim: P4-PGR signaling is critical for SOX4 expression in HESCs.
source: Thus, the P4-PGR signaling was critical for SOX4 expression in HESCs.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that PGR knockdown attenuates SOX4 expression and RU486 blocks MPA-induced SOX4 expression

claim: There is intensive potential PGR binding at SOX4 promoter.
source: Based on previous ATAC-Seq data from undecidualized and decidualized stromal cells and PGR ChIP-Seq from proliferative and secretory endometrium (Chi et al., 2020), we found that there was intensive potential PGR binding at SOX4 promoter (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by ATAC-Seq and PGR ChIP-Seq data from Chi et al., 2020, visualized in Figure 2E

claim: PGR binds to SOX4 promoter in decidualized stromal cells.
source: This speculation was validated by PGR ChIP-qPCR at SOX4 promoter in decidualized stromal cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2F

claim: Overexpression of PGR increases SOX4 promoter reporter activities in the presence of MPA in 293T cells.
source: Furthermore, the binding of PGR on SOX4 promoter was also confirmed by luciferase reporter assay that overexpression of PGR increased the reporter activities in the presence of MPA in 293T cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2G

claim: PGR guides SOX4 expression via direct transcriptional regulation.
source: These results indicated that PGR guided SOX4 expression via direct transcriptional regulation.
evidence: Inferred from PGR binding to SOX4 promoter and increased reporter activity with PGR overexpression

claim: PRL expression is dramatically decreased in SOX4 knockout HESCs after decidualization for 2, 4, and 6 days.
source: The expression of PRL and IGFBP1 was dramatically decreased in SOX4 knockout HESCs after decidualization for 2, 4, and 6 days compared with SOX4 intact cells (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A

claim: IGFBP1 expression is dramatically decreased in SOX4 knockout HESCs after decidualization for 2, 4, and 6 days.
source: The expression of PRL and IGFBP1 was dramatically decreased in SOX4 knockout HESCs after decidualization for 2, 4, and 6 days compared with SOX4 intact cells (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3B-C

claim: SOX4 knockdown by shRNA decreases PRL and IGFBP1 expression in primary HESCs after EPC administration.
source: Similar results were obtained in primary HESC after SOX4 knockdown by shRNA prior to EPC administration (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D

claim: Overexpressing SOX4 in immortalized HESCs significantly augments the expression of PRL and IGFBP1 in decidualized cells.
source: On the other side, overexpressing SOX4 in HESCs significantly augmented the expression of PRL and IGFBP1 in both immortalized (Figure 3D–F) and primary HESC (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C) decidualized for 4 days.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3D-F

claim: Overexpressing SOX4 in primary HESCs significantly augments the expression of PRL and IGFBP1 in decidualized cells.
source: On the other side, overexpressing SOX4 in HESCs significantly augmented the expression of PRL and IGFBP1 in both immortalized (Figure 3D–F) and primary HESC (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C) decidualized for 4 days.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C

claim: SOX4 knockdown results in downregulation of genes critical for decidualization including IGFBP1, PRL, FOXO1, LEFTY2, WNT5A, WNT4, FOSL2, STAT3, IL-11, and BMP2.
source: The genes significantly downregulated after SOX4 knockdown included aforementioned IGFBP1 and PRL as well as other genes critical for decidualization, such as FOXO1, LEFTY2, WNT5A, WNT4, FOSL2, STAT3, LEFTY2, IL-11, and BMP2 (Figure 3G, H).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3G, H

claim: Differentially expressed genes after SOX4 knockdown are enriched in the FOXO signaling pathway, TGF-beta signaling pathway, and MAPK signaling pathway.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis showed that the differentially expressed genes were enriched in the FOXO signaling pathway, TGF-beta signaling pathway, and MAPK signaling pathway (Figure 3I)
evidence: Supported by KEGG analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3I

claim: Differentially expressed genes after SOX4 knockdown are related to autophagy-associated pathway, insulin-like growth factor binding, collagen-containing extracellular matrix, and cell–substrate adhesion.
source: The Gene Ontology (GO) annotation analysis showed that the differentially expressed genes were related to autophagy-associated pathway, insulin-like growth factor binding, collagen-containing extracellular matrix, and cell–substrate adhesion (Figure 3J).
evidence: Supported by GO analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3J

claim: SOX4 plays a critical role in HESCs decidualization.
source: Together, these results revealed the critical role of SOX4 in HESCs decidualization.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing SOX4 knockout/knockdown impairs decidualization markers and SOX4 overexpression enhances them

claim: There are a total of 23,709 SOX4-binding peaks in decidualized stromal cells.
source: Our results showed that there were total of 23,709 SOX4-binding peaks with most of them enriched in promoters, distal intergenic and intron (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 4A

claim: Most SOX4-binding peaks are enriched in promoters, distal intergenic regions, and introns.
source: Our results showed that there were total of 23,709 SOX4-binding peaks with most of them enriched in promoters, distal intergenic and intron (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 4A

claim: SOX4 binding is primarily close to TSS.
source: Peak enrichment indicated that SOX4 binding was primary closed to TSS as well as evidenced by heatmap of peak distribution (Figure 4B, C).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-Seq peak enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B, C

claim: SOX4 mainly binds to genes with higher expression (RPKM ≥1).
source: We also noticed that SOX4 mainly binds to those genes with higher expression (RPKM ≥1) accompanied with few SOX4 binding on those less to no expression genes (RPKM <1) (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-Seq analysis shown in Figure 4B

claim: The most significantly enriched motif at SOX4-binding sites is the SOX4 consensus binding site.
source: Motif analysis results revealed that the most significantly enriched motif was SOX4 consensus binding sites, further supported the reliability of this SOX4 ChIP-Seq.
evidence: Supported by motif analysis of ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 4D

claim: FRA2 and FOSL2 motifs are highly enriched at SOX4-binding sites.
source: We also noticed that FRA2 and FOSL2, two critical members of AP1, were also highly enriched at SOX4-binding sites, indicating the potential cooperation between SOX4 and AP1 (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by motif analysis of ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 4D

claim: 389 genes with SOX4 binding decrease after SOX4 ablation.
source: Considering the correlation between SOX4 binding and gene expression, we overlapped SOX4-binding genes with those downregulated genes after SOX4 knockdown and found that 389 genes with SOX4 binding decreased after SOX4 ablation, indicating the direct regulation of SOX4 on these genes (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by overlap analysis of ChIP-Seq and RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 4E

claim: SOX4 directly regulates 389 genes.
source: Considering the correlation between SOX4 binding and gene expression, we overlapped SOX4-binding genes with those downregulated genes after SOX4 knockdown and found that 389 genes with SOX4 binding decreased after SOX4 ablation, indicating the direct regulation of SOX4 on these genes (Figure 4E).
evidence: Inferred from the overlap of SOX4 binding and downregulated genes after SOX4 knockdown

claim: SOX4 binds to STAT3, FOXO1, and FOSL2 genes.
source: It was gratifying that there were several latent SOX4-binding sites on the STAT3, FOXO1, and FOSL2 in both stromal cell line and primary cultured stromal cells (Figure 4F). ChIP-qPCR also confirmed the binding of SOX4 on these genes (Figure 4G–J).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 4F and ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4G-J

claim: Downregulated genes after SOX4 knockdown possess more SOX4-binding reads compared with upregulated genes.
source: Those downregulated genes (900) after SOX4 knockdown possess more SOX4-binding reads compared with upregulated genes (1022) (Figure 4K)
evidence: Supported by ChIP-Seq analysis shown in Figure 4K

claim: SOX4 has transcriptional activation effects.
source: Those downregulated genes (900) after SOX4 knockdown possess more SOX4-binding reads compared with upregulated genes (1022) (Figure 4K), indicating the transcriptionalactivation effect of SOX4.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that downregulated genes have more SOX4 binding

claim: SOX4 direct target genes show specific enrichment of the FOXO signaling pathway.
source: Importantly, those SOX4 direct target genes also showed specific enrichment of the FOXO signaling pathway (Figure 4L).
evidence: Supported by KEGG analysis shown in Figure 4L

claim: FOXO1 mRNA is overtly decreased when SOX4 is knocked out during decidualization from days 2 to 6.
source: To further assess the regulation of SOX4 on FOXO1, SOX4 was knockout and the expression of FOXO1 was overtly decreased accompanied with compromised decidualization as marked by lessened IGFBP1 during the decidualization from days 2 to 6 (Figure 4M, N).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4M

claim: FOXO1 protein is overtly decreased when SOX4 is knocked out during decidualization from days 2 to 6.
source: To further assess the regulation of SOX4 on FOXO1, SOX4 was knockout and the expression of FOXO1 was overtly decreased accompanied with compromised decidualization as marked by lessened IGFBP1 during the decidualization from days 2 to 6 (Figure 4M, N).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4N

claim: FOXO1 mRNA is upregulated in SOX4 overexpression stromal cells decidualized for 4 days.
source: On the other hand, FOXO1 mRNA and protein were upregulated in SOX4 overexpression stromal cell decidualized for 4 days, as well as IGFBP1 protein (Figure 4O, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4O

claim: FOXO1 protein is upregulated in SOX4 overexpression stromal cells decidualized for 4 days.
source: On the other hand, FOXO1 mRNA and protein were upregulated in SOX4 overexpression stromal cell decidualized for 4 days, as well as IGFBP1 protein (Figure 4O, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B

claim: The effects of SOX4 overexpression on decidualization are blocked when FOXO1 is knocked down.
source: Moreover, the effects of SOX4 overexpression on decidualization were blocked when the FOXO1 was knockdown, suggested the FOXO1 as a crucial effector downstream of SOX4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B

claim: FOXO1 is a crucial effector downstream of SOX4.
source: Moreover, the effects of SOX4 overexpression on decidualization were blocked when the FOXO1 was knockdown, suggested the FOXO1 as a crucial effector downstream of SOX4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Inferred from the observation that FOXO1 knockdown blocks SOX4 overexpression effects

claim: SOX4 directly regulates transcription of transcription factor FOXO1.
source: In summary, these results suggested that SOX4 directly regulated transcription of transcription factor FOXO1, as well as other molecules conducive for human endometrial decidualization.
evidence: Inferred from SOX4 binding to FOXO1 and regulation of FOXO1 expression

claim: PGR protein levels (both PRA and PRB isoforms) are dramatically decreased in the absence of SOX4 on days 0, 2, 3, and 6 during decidualization.
source: We were attracted by the finding that PGR protein levels, including both the PRA and PRB isoforms, were dramatically decreased in the absence of SOX4 on days 0, 2, 3, and 6 during the decidualization without overt transcription reduction (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5B

claim: PGR mRNA levels do not show overt reduction in the absence of SOX4 during decidualization.
source: We were attracted by the finding that PGR protein levels, including both the PRA and PRB isoforms, were dramatically decreased in the absence of SOX4 on days 0, 2, 3, and 6 during the decidualization without overt transcription reduction (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5A

claim: SOX4 stabilizes PGR protein at post-transcriptional level.
source: Similar results were also observed in primary stromal cells, implying that SOX4 stabled PGR protein at post-transcriptional level (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Inferred from decreased PGR protein without mRNA reduction in SOX4-deficient cells

claim: Treatment with proteasome inhibitor MG-132 efficiently attenuates the rapid degradation of PGR protein in SOX4-deficient cells.
source: Furthermore, treatment of cells with the proteasome inhibitor MG-132 for 6 hr efficiently attenuated the rapid degradation of PGR protein in SOX4-deficient cells (Figure 5C)
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C

claim: Autophagy inhibitor 3-MA cannot rescue or attenuate the degradation of PGR protein in SOX4-deficient cells.
source: but the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) cannot rescue or attenuate the degradation of PGR protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: PGR protein is mainly degraded through the proteasome in the absence of SOX4.
source: but the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) cannot rescue or attenuate the degradation of PGR protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggested the PGR protein was mainly degraded through the proteasome in the absence of SOX4.
evidence: Inferred from MG-132 rescuing PGR degradation but 3-MA not rescuing it

claim: PGR protein degeneration is faster in SOX4-depleted HESCs in the presence of cycloheximide.
source: Likewise, PGR protein degeneration was faster in SOX4-depleted HESCs 2 days after EPC treatment in the presence of the protein synthesis inhibitor cycloheximide (CHX) for 0, 3, 6, and 9 hr (Figure 5D, E).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5D, E

claim: SOX4 knockdown leads to shortened half-life of PGR protein.
source: Thus, these results revealed that SOX4 knockdown led to shortened the half-life of PGR protein.
evidence: Inferred from faster PGR degradation in SOX4-depleted cells treated with CHX

claim: PGR ubiquitination is increased after SOX4 depletion.
source: Notably, PGR ubiquitination was increased after SOX4 depletion (Figure 5F).
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 5F

claim: SOX4 knockdown reduces PGR protein stability through the polyubiquitin-mediated proteasome degradation pathway.
source: These results suggested that SOX4 knockdown reduced PGR protein stability through the polyubiquitin-mediated proteasome degradation pathway.
evidence: Inferred from increased PGR ubiquitination and proteasome-dependent degradation in SOX4-deficient cells

claim: HERC4, RNF213, and UBR3 are E3 ubiquitination ligases identified by mass spectrometry of PGR immunoprecipitated proteins.
source: Reassuringly, several E3 ubiquitination ligases were identified, including HERC4, RNF213, and UBR3 whose expressions were also upregulated according to RNA-Seq in SOX4-silenced HESCs (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6A

claim: HERC4, RNF213, and UBR3 expressions are upregulated in SOX4-silenced HESCs.
source: Reassuringly, several E3 ubiquitination ligases were identified, including HERC4, RNF213, and UBR3 whose expressions were also upregulated according to RNA-Seq in SOX4-silenced HESCs (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 6A

claim: HERC4 mRNA is upregulated when SOX4 is downregulated.
source: Real-time PCR confirmed the abnormal upregulation of these E3 ligases when SOX4 was downregulated (Figure 6B, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6B

claim: HERC4 protein level is upregulated upon the ablation of SOX4.
source: The protein level of HERC4 was consistently upregulated upon the ablation of SOX4 (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6C

claim: HERC4 interacts with PGR as a potential E3 ubiquitin ligase.
source: As HERC4 showed the most significant change after SOX4 knockdown and its interaction with PGR as a potential E3 ubiquitin ligase was also supported by UbiBrowser database (http://ubibrowser.ncpsb.org), we mainly focused on this E3 ligase in our following experiments.
evidence: Supported by UbiBrowser database prediction

claim: There is a conserved physical interaction between endogenous HERC4 and PGR in decidualized stromal cells.
source: The coimmunoprecipitation result demonstrated a conserved physical interaction between endogenous HERC4 and PGR in decidualized stromal cells as well asexogenous expressed in 293T cells (Figure 6D, E).
evidence: Supported by coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6D, E

claim: HERC4 and PGR colocalize in decidualized HESCs.
source: Immunoﬂuorescence analysis showed the colocalization of HERC4 and PGR in decidualized HESCs (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6F

claim: Overexpression of HERC4 increases PGR ubiquitination.
source: To figure out whether HERC4 could induce endogenous ubiquitination of PGR, HERC4 was overexpressed in immortalized HESCs followed by decidualization for 2 days. The ubiquitination of PGR was higher in the presence of HERC4 than in control, as shown in Figure 6G
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 6G

claim: HERC4 abolished by siRNA significantly reduces PGR ubiquitination in 293T cells.
source: Conversely, HERC4 abolished by siRNA significantly reduced PGR ubiquitination in 293T cells (Figure 6H).
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 6H

claim: HERC4 is a critical E3 ligase for PGR ubiquitination.
source: The above studies demonstrated that HERC4 was a critical E3 ligase for PGR ubiquitination.
evidence: Inferred from HERC4 overexpression increasing and HERC4 knockdown decreasing PGR ubiquitination

claim: Overexpression of HERC4 rescues the decreasing PGR ubiquitination in the presence of SOX4 in 293T cells.
source: Moreover, overexpression of HERC4 recused the decreasing PGR ubiquitination in the presence of SOX4 in 293T cells (Figure 6I).
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 6I

claim: SOX4 affects PGR ubiquitination through E3 ubiquitin ligase HERC4.
source: Hence, SOX4 affected PGR ubiquitination through E3 ubiquitin ligase HERC4.
evidence: Inferred from HERC4 overexpression rescuing PGR ubiquitination in the presence of SOX4

claim: HERC4 overexpression decreases PGR protein level in 293T cells.
source: This posit was underpinned by decreased PGR protein level with HERC4 overexpression in both 293T cells (Figure 6J) and immortalized HESCs (Figure 6K).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6J

claim: HERC4 overexpression decreases PGR protein level in immortalized HESCs.
source: This posit was underpinned by decreased PGR protein level with HERC4 overexpression in both 293T cells (Figure 6J) and immortalized HESCs (Figure 6K).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6K

claim: PGR protein is rescued by siRNA-mediated knockdown of HERC4 in SOX4 abolished decidualized immortalized HESCs.
source: PGR protein was also rescued by siRNA-mediated knockdown of HERC4 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E) in SOX4 abolished decidualized immortalized HESCs (Figure 6L)
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6L

claim: IGFBP1 level is rescued by HERC4 knockdown in SOX4 abolished decidualized immortalized HESCs.
source: and consistently, the IGFBP1 level was also rescued (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F

claim: PGR half-life increases after HERC4 repression in normal immortalized HESCs.
source: Likewise, PGR half-life increased in both normal and SOX4 abolished immortalized HESCs after HERC4 repression (Figure 6M, N).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6M, N

claim: PGR half-life increases after HERC4 repression in SOX4 abolished immortalized HESCs.
source: Likewise, PGR half-life increased in both normal and SOX4 abolished immortalized HESCs after HERC4 repression (Figure 6M, N).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6M, N

claim: SOX4 mediates PGR degradation by modulating E3 ligase HERC4.
source: In a word, these studies demonstrated that SOX4-mediated PGR degradation by modulating E3 ligase HERC4.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing HERC4 knockdown rescues PGR levels in SOX4-deficient cells

claim: Only F3 (DBD domain of PGR) exhibits protein degradation after cotransfection with HERC4 in 293T cells.

claim: K588, K613, K617, and K638 are critical for PGR degradation.
source: Point mutation of all Lysine (K) to arginine (R) in DBD region (Figure 7C) showed that K588, K613, K617, and K638 were critical for PGR degradation (Figure 7D)
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7D

claim: K588, K613, K617, and K638 are vital for PGR ubiquitination by HERC4.
source: which was further sustained by incapable PGR ubiquitination mediated by HERC4 in these mutant forms when compared with WT or K565R in 293T cells (Figure 7E). Collective, these results suggested that K588, K613, K617, and K638 were vital for PGR ubiquitination by HERC4.
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 7E

claim: SOX4 expression is significantly decreased in the mid-secretory endometrium of women with EMS-RIF compared to healthy women.

claim: FOXO1 expression is significantly decreased in the mid-secretory endometrium of women with EMS-RIF compared to healthy women.
source: The expressions of SOX4, FOXO1, IGFBP1, and PRL were significantly decreased in EMS-RIF group with increased HERC4 compared with the control, but the mRNA level of PGR was comparable in both groups (Figure 8A–F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8B

claim: IGFBP1 expression is significantly decreased in the mid-secretory endometrium of women with EMS-RIF compared to healthy women.
source: The expressions of SOX4, FOXO1, IGFBP1, and PRL were significantly decreased in EMS-RIF group with increased HERC4 compared with the control, but the mRNA level of PGR was comparable in both groups (Figure 8A–F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8C

claim: PRL expression is significantly decreased in the mid-secretory endometrium of women with EMS-RIF compared to healthy women.
source: The expressions of SOX4, FOXO1, IGFBP1, and PRL were significantly decreased in EMS-RIF group with increased HERC4 compared with the control, but the mRNA level of PGR was comparable in both groups (Figure 8A–F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8D

claim: HERC4 expression is increased in the mid-secretory endometrium of women with EMS-RIF compared to healthy women.
source: The expressions of SOX4, FOXO1, IGFBP1, and PRL were significantly decreased in EMS-RIF group with increased HERC4 compared with the control, but the mRNA level of PGR was comparable in both groups (Figure 8A–F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8F

claim: PGR mRNA level is comparable between healthy women and women with EMS-RIF.
source: The expressions of SOX4, FOXO1, IGFBP1, and PRL were significantly decreased in EMS-RIF group with increased HERC4 compared with the control, but the mRNA level of PGR was comparable in both groups (Figure 8A–F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8E

claim: A large portion of endometrial samples from women with EMS-RIF show reduced expression of SOX4, FOXO1, and IGFBP1 at protein level.
source: At protein level, a large portion of endometrial samples from women with EMS-RIF showed reduced expression of SOX4, FOXO1, and IGFBP1.

claim: PGR protein is significantly decreased in women with EMS-RIF despite comparable mRNA levels.

claim: HERC4 protein is increased in women with EMS-RIF.

claim: PGR, SOX4, IGFBP1, and FOXO1 expression are significantly reduced in stromal cells of women with EMS-RIF.
source: Immunostaining analysis further revealed significantly reduced PGR, SOX4, IGFBP1, and FOXO1 expression and increased HERC4 in stromal cells in women with EMS-RIF (Figure 8I).

claim: HERC4 expression is increased in stromal cells of women with EMS-RIF.

claim: SOX4, FOXO1, PGR, and IGFBP1 expression levels are lower in primary HESCs of EMS-RIF cultured with EPC for 4 days compared to control.

claim: Adequate crosstalk between implantation-competent embryo and receptive endometrium is prerequisite for successful pregnancy.
